You are helping a user write SQL queries to a database. If something is not clear, you can ask the user to clarify what they need. The schema for the database being accessed is the following:
        
CREATE TABLE employee (
    Employee_ID INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    Name TEXT,
    Age INT,
    City TEXT,
    UNIQUE (Employee_ID)
);

CREATE TABLE shop (
    Shop_ID INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    Name TEXT,
    Location TEXT,
    District TEXT,
    Number_products INT,
    Manager_name TEXT,
    UNIQUE (Shop_ID)
);

CREATE TABLE hiring (
    Shop_ID INT,
    Employee_ID INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    Start_from TEXT,
    Is_full_time bool,
    UNIQUE (Employee_ID),
    FOREIGN KEY (Employee_ID) REFERENCES employee(Employee_ID),
    FOREIGN KEY (Shop_ID) REFERENCES shop(Shop_ID)
);

CREATE TABLE evaluation (
    Employee_ID TEXT   PRIMARY KEY,
    Year_awarded TEXT   PRIMARY KEY,
    Bonus REAL,
    PRIMARY KEY (Employee_ID, Year_awarded),
    UNIQUE (Employee_ID, Year_awarded),
    FOREIGN KEY (Employee_ID) REFERENCES employee(Employee_ID)
);

```sql
-- Stores with many products (highest product counts)
SELECT
  Shop_ID,
  Name,
  Location,
  District,
  Number_products
FROM shop
ORDER BY Number_products DESC;
```

If you mean “many” as in “above a threshold”, tell me the cutoff (e.g., > 100), or use:

```sql
SELECT
  Shop_ID, Name, Location, District, Number_products
FROM shop
WHERE Number_products >= 100
ORDER BY Number_products DESC;
```
stores with more than average products would be interesting

```sql
SELECT
  Shop_ID,
  Name,
  Location,
  District,
  Number_products
FROM shop
WHERE Number_products > (SELECT AVG(Number_products) FROM shop)
ORDER BY Number_products DESC;
```
there's a way to look at stores that exceed a certain number of products

```sql
-- Stores exceeding a given product threshold
SELECT
  Shop_ID,
  Name,
  Location,
  District,
  Number_products
FROM shop
WHERE Number_products > :min_products
ORDER BY Number_products DESC;
```

Replace `:min_products` with a number (e.g., `200`), or with `?` / `$1` depending on your SQL tool.
you should also pull the names of those stores too

```sql
SELECT
  Shop_ID,
  Name AS Store_Name,
  Location,
  District,
  Number_products
FROM shop
WHERE Number_products > :min_products
ORDER BY Number_products DESC, Name;
```
there's a focus on how many products each store has

```sql
-- Focused view: product counts per store (optionally filter by a threshold)
SELECT
  Name AS Store_Name,
  Number_products
FROM shop
WHERE Number_products > :min_products   -- remove this line if you want all stores
ORDER BY Number_products DESC, Store_Name;
```
